conviction_note: Evidence is two-sided: DayOne-stake risk (BIS rule of 2026-11-16 hitting a 69%-ByteDance, Johor-heavy affiliate whose IPO was due in November), an AI-infra sell-off and Alibaba's possible 20GW cut on the downside, against a stock that is already -40% in 20 days, -71% from its high, with rising short interest (~10.6% of float), strong Q3 hyperscaler capex and an August 'major business win in the current quarter' remark on the upside. The findings sum to +1.2 but p_up stays at 52 because the 6.3-point put skew and an unsourced quarterly bar pull it toward 50; abs_move is 10, above the 7.3% event-implied move, because realised vol is 104% and the confirmed prints moved -9.3% and +6.2%.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue: chartmill about RMB3.191bn (https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/GDS/estimates, from search snippet) vs Benzinga $474.4M (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/GDS/earnings-forecasts) and MarketBeat-based $468.7M. The USD and RMB figures disagree (at about 7.1, $474M is about RMB3.37bn), so the quarterly bar is disputed and every reported-quarter finding is capped small. The company's own FY2026 guide is revenue RMB12.7-13.0bn and adj. EBITDA RMB5.9-6.1bn (6-K ex99-1, 2026-08-13, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001526125/000110465926095498/tm2621440d1_ex99-1.htm). With H1 revenue at RMB6.455bn, that implies H2 of RMB6.245-6.545bn, about RMB3.12-3.27bn a quarter, so RMB3.19bn sits at the guide midpoint. The EPS consensus of $1.31 (Earnings Whispers/Benzinga) mixes currencies and is unusable.
positioning_check: Short interest was 14.54M ADS at the 2026-10-30 settlement, up from 13.74M the month before. That is about 10.6% of the 136.68M float, with days to cover of 5.5 (stockanalysis, updated 2026-11-24, https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/gds/statistics/) or 6.2 (massive.com, https://massive.com/quote/gds.md). The November settlement was not found. Baseline: 25-delta skew +6.34 vol points (downside paid), put/call OI 0.70, ATM IV 108%, event-implied move 7.33%, ATM spread 25% of mid. The short is rising and moderately crowded into a stock that is -40% in 20 days; it rose +13.4% on 2026-11-23 and fell about -10% on 2026-11-24, which shows a violent two-way reflex.

The other baseline rows (03-17, 04-30, 05-06, 06-02, 07-30, 11-12) are not confirmed earnings events; 11-12 was the day after the date-notice 6-K.

expectations.real_bar: The stock rises only if Q3 bookings show visible progress toward the 1GW target (a large Q3 win, with the target reaffirmed) AND management defuses the DayOne/BIS-rule and AI-capex overhang (for example by quantifying the ByteDance exposure, giving an IPO path, or showing domestic chip supply and move-ins on track). An in-line revenue print by itself is not the bar.

next_guide.company_current_guide: FY2026 revenue RMB12,700-13,000m, adj. EBITDA RMB5,900-6,100m, capex about RMB10,000m, all raised 2026-08-13 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001526125/000110465926095498/tm2621440d1_ex99-1.htm); bookings target 1GW for 2026; FY2027 guide normally given around March
next_guide.basis: Annual guidance was raised only three months ago and the company guides annually in March. Q3 consensus (about RMB3.19bn) sits at the implied H2 run-rate. Peer VNET maintained its FY guide on 2026-11-23 while trimming capex. So the most likely outcome is a reaffirmation, with the 1GW bookings target as the real swing item.

findings.finding: Into the print GDS is -40.2% over 20 days and -16.8% over 5, $13.65 against sell-side targets of $45-55 with no target cut found since August. Short interest rose to 14.54M ADS (about 10.6% of float, 5.5-6.2 days to cover) at the 2026-10-30 settlement, and the stock showed a +13.4% one-day reflex on 2026-11-23. Expectations on the China core business are deeply reset, so an adequate bookings/DayOne answer has room to squeeze.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Confirmed prints: Q1 2026 -9.28% despite record bookings (sold into strength after a run), Q2 2026 +6.2% on a guide raise. Both after less washed-out setups.
findings.why_not_priced: The washed-out level is priced by definition. What is not priced is the asymmetry: shorts kept building into a stock already -71% from its high. If the market expected a clean print, short interest would be falling and the skew would not be bid; both point the other way.
findings.independence: Price path from the sealed baseline; rising shorts from https://massive.com/quote/gds.md; targets from https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/gds/ratings/; the +13.4% reflex on 11-23 from massive.com. These are separate sources, but all of them are positioning, not fundamentals.

findings.finding: On the 2026-08-13 call management said GDS was 'well on the way to securing a further major business win' in Q3. That came after 260MW of bookings in Q2 and 470MW in H1 against a newly doubled 1GW FY target, which needs about 530MW in H2. A large Q3 booking is the line the preview says the stock must prove.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Record bookings of about 200MW in Q1 2026 were sold (-9.28%); the 1GW target raise in Q2 was bought (+6.2%).
findings.why_not_priced: The stock has halved since the statement, which means the market now doubts the 1GW conversion (the preview says analysts are unwilling to credit it). If the win were priced, the stock would not sit 6% above its post-earnings low going into the print.
findings.independence: Bookings figures confirmed by https://quartr.com/events/gds-holdings-limited-gds-q2-2026_3POfHdDS and the 6-K. The 'major win' remark has one source (the transcript).

findings.finding: On 2026-11-16 BIS issued an interim final rule requiring licences for AI-chip exports to overseas data centres that serve China-headquartered companies, with a 90-day transition and extra licensing for Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil. That hits DayOne (GDS holds about 19.4%, valued above $2.2B at the Series C, against a GDS market cap of about $2.7-4.5B): 69% of its revenue is ByteDance and about 1.4GW of its bookings are in Johor. Its US IPO was slated for November and had already been reported in October as possibly scaled to $2.5-3B or delayed. The call is the first place management can address the stake's value and the IPO path.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No earnings-day precedent. DayOne value events have moved the stock before: the Q1 2026 stake sale and the Q2 dilution gain both fell on earnings days (-9.3%, +6.2%). The stock fell -12.1% on the day the rule was announced.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: -12.1% on 11-16 and about -32% since 11-06. What is not priced is management's answer, which is either an IPO postponement or impairment talk (more downside) or a quantified 'ByteDance work is not AI training, under 50% of 2027 commitments' reassurance (relief). Skew bid suggests the market leans to the former.
findings.independence: DayOne's ByteDance and Johor exposure from https://dealroom.co/news/info-5pbeiz-singapores-dayone-pushes-ahead-with-data-center-ipo-tied-to-tiktok/ and https://sovereignmagazine.com/article/dayone-nasdaq-ipo-filing-johor-revenue; IPO scale-back reports from https://m.chinaventure.com.cn/news/113-20261022-393715.html; the -12.1% on 11-16 from goldesel.de. The rule and the exposure come from different sources; no source ties the rule to DayOne directly.

findings.finding: GDS's hyperscaler customer base spent sharply more in the September quarter: Tencent capex was RMB81.4bn (+54% QoQ, +527% YoY, reported 2026-11-18) and Alibaba capex was RMB50.5bn (+60% YoY, reported 2026-11-18/19). That supports domestic wholesale data-centre demand in the quarter GDS reports.
findings.link: Chinese hyperscalers (Alibaba, Tencent, ByteDance) are GDS's principal wholesale customers; GDS attributes its record bookings to hyperscaler AI demand. The exact revenue share is not sourced here.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None isolated for this name; the stock fell through both hyperscaler prints anyway.
findings.why_not_priced: Hyperscaler capex is mostly chips and servers, not third-party leasing, so the market has not transmitted it to GDS (the stock fell through both reports). If priced, GDS would have rallied with the capex prints.
findings.independence: Alibaba capex from https://stockanalysis.com/news/baba-q2-fy2027-earnings-revenue-beat/ (2026-11-19). This is a proxy: capex to leasing is not confirmed by GDS.

findings.finding: On its 2026-11-19 call Alibaba said the new US compute export rules 'may' lead to a downward revision of its 20GW-by-2032 capacity target, with an associated capex reduction. No number was given. It is a negative read-across for Chinese data-centre demand sentiment.
findings.link: Alibaba is one of GDS's large hyperscaler customers; the 20GW target is global and the domestic/overseas split is not given.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: GDS fell further after 11-19. GDS management will be asked whether Alibaba's domestic orders change; the answer is not in the price.
findings.independence: https://magica.com/news/alibaba-cloud-growth-outlook-capacity-target reports the same remark. The rule restricts OVERSEAS compute, which could push Chinese demand back onshore toward GDS; that cuts against this finding's sign, so it is sized small.

findings.finding: Peer VNET reported Q3 2026 on 2026-11-23: revenue +14.8%, adj. EBITDA +21.7%, FY guide maintained, a 60MW order from a leading cloud provider, committed capacity up from 970MW to 1,095MW. FY capex fell to RMB8-10bn from RMB10-12bn and wholesale utilisation dipped from 73.9% to 70.7%. GDS rose 13.4% that day.
findings.link: Same market (Chinese wholesale data centres), the same hyperscaler customers and the same chip-supply dependence; VNET's wholesale revenue grew 27.6%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: GDS +13.4% on VNET's print day, then about -10% the next day.
findings.why_not_priced: GDS's +13.4% and -10% round trip suggests the read-across was priced and then given back. Residual information: demand intact, but VNET slowed its build (a capex cut), which is mixed for GDS.
findings.independence: The GDS price reaction from https://massive.com/quote/gds.md; the VNET numbers from its own 6-K.

findings.finding: FY2026 guidance (revenue RMB12.7-13.0bn, adj. EBITDA RMB5.9-6.1bn) was raised on 2026-08-13 and the FY street revenue (about $1.84B) still sits below its low end. A reaffirmation therefore clears a street that does not believe the guide; annual guidance normally comes in March, so a change now is unlikely.
findings.why_not_priced: The street's FY figure below the guide floor shows disbelief (or a currency artefact); a reaffirmation would be mildly better than street. Small because the gap may be FX conversion.

findings.finding: Q3 revenue consensus (chartmill about RMB3.19bn) sits at the guide-implied H2 run-rate of RMB3.12-3.27bn a quarter. Q2 revenue was RMB3.088bn, with 145MW of H1 move-ins feeding Q3 and only 90MW guided for H2, so revenue is likely in line. Management guided a roughly 3% YoY decline in monthly service revenue per sqm by Q4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue was a slight miss on Q2 (on Earnings Whispers' conversion) and the stock still rose +6.2%; revenue is not the line this stock trades on.
findings.why_not_priced: Inside what the company already guided, so mostly priced. Capped small because the quarterly bar is disputed (the USD and RMB consensus disagree).

findings.finding: Q2 net income of RMB837.6m was driven by a RMB959.9m DayOne dilution gain, and Q1 by a stake-sale gain. With no Series C event in Q3 and DayOne loss-making (H1 net loss $77.2m), Q3 GAAP net income will likely fall sharply QoQ. Aggregators that set RMB EPS against a USD $1.31 consensus may headline a large 'miss'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Earnings Whispers headlined Q2 as a 61.5% EPS 'miss' through currency mixing; the stock rose +6.2% anyway.
findings.why_not_priced: It is below operating income with no path to guidance; only a headline-algo effect at the open.
findings.independence: The DayOne gain is in the 6-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001526125/000110465926095498/tm2621440d1_ex99-1.htm); DayOne's H1 loss from https://technode.global/2026/10/06/singapore-based-china-originated-dayone-data-centers-widens-net-loss-in-h1-2026-to-77-2m/.

findings.finding: AI-infrastructure financing is being repriced across the sector: on 2026-11-12 GDS fell 12.7% on credit concerns around US AI cloud operators. GDS is levered (net debt/EBITDA about 4.7x per the preview, 5.1-5.3x on guidance), raised capex to RMB10bn weighted to H2, and funds about 60% of projects with debt.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: -11.36% to -12.7% on 2026-11-12 with no company news.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced in the -40%. The residual is whether the call raises capex again or signals funding needs. Per the financing lesson, capex that funds record bookings is not a distress signal, hence small.
findings.independence: https://koalagains.com/daily-top-movers/top-losers/details/eb805f47-7627-4e93-9259-630d607662dc attributes the same day to export-control fears; https://www.caiwennews.com/article/1688474.shtml describes sector repricing to 'capex scrutiny' (2026-11-06).

findings.finding: The first post-IPO asset injection into GDS's C-REIT was 'under regulatory review' with no timing given on the Q2 call, and guidance excludes further monetisation. An approval or completion announced with Q3 would be a deleveraging positive; no update was found.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The C-REIT IPO in 2025 coincided with positive prints; nothing isolated.
findings.why_not_priced: Timing is unknown. If the market expected approval, leverage concerns would not be part of the sell-off narrative.
findings.independence: The 2026-11-18 preview says it is still under review (https://finviz.com/news/424958/gds-must-prove-its-1-gigawatt-bookings-surge-is-real-after-stock-halves).

outside_window.finding: DayOne US IPO (DODC) pricing or a formal postponement; no price range or roadshow found as of 2026-11-24. It sets the market value of GDS's about 19.4% stake.

outside_window.finding: The BIS rule's 90-day transition for existing data-centre arrangements serving China-HQ firms (licence deadline about mid-February 2027) decides DayOne's ByteDance capacity.
FY2027 guidance is normally given around March 2027; management guided 2027 move-ins to more than double, weighted to H2.

baseline_tension: The put skew (+6.34) and -40% run-up say downside. My findings are mixed and lean slightly up, because the decline appears to have priced the DayOne/BIS shock and the sector de-rating while short interest keeps rising, so p_up is held only marginally above 50 rather than leaning against the skew with conviction.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): the Q3 bookings finding cut from +1.0 to +0.7, because record Q1 bookings were sold (-9.28%).
Lesson 5 (a proxy is smaller): hyperscaler capex as a proxy for GDS leasing cut from +0.8 to +0.6; GDS has not confirmed the transmission.
Lesson 6 (verify the bar): the quarterly bar is disputed (USD vs RMB consensus disagree), so reported-quarter findings stay capped at 0.2-0.3; no change in size, recorded in bar.
FPI history lesson: base rate rebuilt from the two confirmed 2026 prints (-9.28%, +6.2%); the other baseline rows were not used. abs_move kept at 10 given 104% realised vol.
Lesson 7 (positioning): a slightly positive sign against a +6.3 skew is justified by rising short interest and a -40% run-up, but p_up kept at 52, not higher.

Left standing: the DayOne/BIS regulatory negative (-1.0), the Alibaba counterparty negative, the macro/financing negative (financing lesson: the capex funds bookings, so kept small) and the one-off sized as a one-off.
